sections.h2: Three Ways to Start a Video
paras: You do not need to learn prompt engineering before the first video. Start from whatever you already have — a product page, a photo, or a creative brief — and the workspace handles the rest.
**URL to Video** turns a public product page into an ad or demo video. Paste a link and the import fills in the product name, photos and details; check them, then choose the presenter and format.
**Image to Video** starts from one product photo. Add a short scene description and the model animates the product; a clear photo with the label visible produces the most usable clip.
**Text to Video** converts a written brief into an editable storyboard, then generates the shots you keep. It is the right entry when you have a message but no usable photo yet.

The [video ads generator](/ai-video-generation/video-ads) takes your input and produces the four layers a short ad needs: the script, written as spoken lines rather than ad copy; a presenter who holds or wears the product and talks to camera; the voiceover; and the finish — captions and the frame size you picked, 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts by default.

You still make the decisions that matter: which presenter, what the first three seconds say, how long the clip runs, and whether the product stays the hero. The difference is that changing your mind costs a rerun, not a reshoot.
Every job shows its credit cost before it starts. Files download without a watermark, and a failed job returns its credits to your balance automatically.
**AI Actor** pairs an avatar from the directory with your script and voiceover — UGC-style talking-head video without cameras, casting, or a studio.

**AI Twin** creates a digital clone that looks, speaks and moves like the person it is built from. Use it for founder-led content and personal brands where the face has to be consistent across every clip.
**AI Presenter** covers demos and explainers: product walkthroughs, feature callouts and social content delivered in a natural, conversational register.
The goal is not to replace UGC with polished studio production. It is to keep the fast hook, the conversational delivery, the product proof and the clear call to action that make creator video work.

Videos are priced by length: a 15-second clip costs 20 credits and a 30-second clip costs 40. A single product photo costs 1 credit. The quote appears before the job starts, so there is no surprise on the invoice.

Packages are one-time purchases with credits delivered monthly for the term: Starter is $24 for 200 credits a month, Pro is $59 for 500, and Studio is $129 for 1,200. Six- and twelve-month terms cost less per month, and credit packs are open to everyone when a month runs short.
There is no subscription and no auto-renewal. If a job fails, its credits return to your balance automatically.
**Ecommerce and D2C brands** testing new creative every week: each variant costs credits instead of a shoot day.
**Dropshippers and small businesses** that need a product explainer without booking a crew: one photo is enough to start.
**Marketers and agencies** that want "waiting on assets" off the media-plan critical path: the same product can be re-cut for TikTok, Reels, Shorts, and feed placements.
**Content creators, apps and SaaS teams** shipping launch videos and feature demos with a consistent presenter and voice.

Producing a UGC-style product video has traditionally meant booking a shoot, casting a creator, and waiting on editing. AIVideosUGC compresses that into opening a link, uploading an image, or writing a sentence — the difference between a campaign that waits on assets and one that ships on schedule.
"AI UGC video should start with a link, not a six-month pilot," says Naruebet Nakphong, founder of BLYDEY INC. Start with what you have, check the cost, and post the first ad this week.
